studies.title: ARA 290, a nonerythropoietic peptide engineered from erythropoietin, improves metabolic control and neuropathic symptoms in patients with type 2 diabetes.
studies.abstract: Although erythropoietin ameliorates experimental type 2 diabetes with neuropathy, serious side effects limit its potential clinical use. ARA 290, a nonhematopoietic peptide designed from the structure of erythropoietin, interacts selectively with the innate repair receptor that mediates tissue protection. ARA 290 has shown efficacy in preclinical and clinical studies of metabolic control and neuropathy. To evaluate the potential activity of ARA 290 in type 2 diabetes and painful neuropathy, subjects were enrolled in this phase 2 study. ARA 290 (4 mg) or placebo were self-administered subcutaneously daily for 28 d and the subjects followed for an additional month without further treatment. No potential safety issues were identified. Subjects receiving ARA 290 exhibited an improvement in hemoglobin A(1c) (Hb A(1c)) and lipid profiles throughout the 56 d observation period. Neuropathic symptoms as assessed by the PainDetect questionnaire improved significantly in the ARA 290 group. Mean corneal nerve fiber density (CNFD) was reduced significantly compared with normal controls and subjects with a mean CNFD >1 standard deviation from normal showed a significant increase in CNFD compared with no change in the placebo group. These observations suggest that ARA 290 may benefit both metabolic control and neuropathy in subjects with type 2 diabetes and deserves continued clinical evaluation.

studies.title: ARA 290 improves symptoms in patients with sarcoidosis-associated small nerve fiber loss and increases corneal nerve fiber density.

studies.title: Safety and efficacy of ARA 290 in sarcoidosis patients with symptoms of small fiber neuropathy: a randomized, double-blind pilot study.
studies.abstract: ARA 290 (a peptide designed to activate the innate repair receptor that arrests injury and initiates cytoprotection, antiinflammation and healing) reduces allodynia in preclinical neuropathy models. We studied the safety and efficacy of ARA 290 to reduce symptoms of small fiber neuropathy (SFN) in patients with sarcoidosis. A total of 22 patients diagnosed with sarcoidosis and symptoms of SFN were enrolled in a double-blind, placebo-controlled exploratory trial consisting of three times weekly intravenous dosing of ARA 290 (2 mg; n = 12) or placebo (n = 10) for 4 wks. Inclusion criteria were a diagnosis of neuropathy and a spontaneous pain score of ≥5 (Brief Pain Inventory [BPI]). Endpoints assessed were changes in pain intensity and the small fiber neuropathy screening list (SFNSL) score, quality of life (SF-36), depressive symptoms (Inventory of Depressive Symptomatology [IDS]) and fatigue (Fatigue Assessment Scale [FAS]). No safety concerns were raised by clinical or laboratory assessments. The ARA 290 group showed significant (p < 0.05) improvement at wk 4 in SFNSL score compared with placebo (Δ -11.5 ± 3.04 versus Δ -2.9 ± 3.34 [standard error of the mean]). Additionally, the ARA 290 group showed a significant change from baseline in the pain and physical functioning dimensions of the SF-36 (Δ -23.4 ± 5.5 and Δ -14.6 ± 3.9, respectively). The mean BPI and FAS scores improved significantly but equivalently in both patient groups. No change was observed in the IDS. ARA 290 appears to be safe in patients with sarcoidosis and can reduce neuropathic symptoms.

studies.title: Immunometabolic dysregulation drives selective executive cognitive dysfunction in male db/db mice.
studies.abstract: Type 2 diabetes (T2D) is associated with cognitive impairment, with executive functions such as cognitive flexibility being particularly vulnerable. Growing evidence suggests that chronic inflammatory and metabolic stress contributes to diabetes -related brain dysfunction, yet behavioral assessment in animal models is often confounded by anxiety, altered motivation, and reduced response vigor. In this study, we used a translational touchscreen-based operant platform to distinguish associative learning from executive cognitive flexibility in db/db mice, a well-established genetic model of T2D, and to evaluate the effects of the non-erythropoietic erythropoietin derived peptide ARA 290. Male db/db mice and age matched db/m heterozygote lean controls were tested using pairwise visual discrimination to assess associative learning and reversal learning to probe cognitive flexibility. Metabolic function was evaluated using glucose and insulin tolerance tests, while immune and metabolic effects of ARA 290 were evaluated by flow cytometry and RNA-seq. Db/db mice displayed delayed task engagement and longer response latencies during pretraining and acquisition, yet maintained intact associative learning accuracy. In contrast, they exhibited pronounced impairments in cognitive flexibility during reversal learning, characterized by increased perseveration and reduced adaptation to changed reward contingencies. Treatment with ARA 290 improved insulin sensitivity and altered circulating monocyte proportions but did not rescue deficits in executive cognitive flexibility. RNA-seq of the hippocampus revealed enrichment of immune pathways consistent with chronic low-grade inflammation, providing molecular context for the observed behavioral phenotype. Together, these findings demonstrate that T2D selectively impairs executive cognitive flexibility while sparing basic associative learning, and that improvement in peripheral metabolic function and altered monocyte proportions are insufficient to restore executive cognition. This work highlights the value of touchscreen-based paradigms for resolving distinct cognitive domains in metabolic disease and highlights the need to target brain specific immunometabolic mechanisms to address diabetes-associated cognitive dysfunction.

studies.title: Early monocyte modulation by the non-erythropoietic peptide ARA 290 decelerates AD-like pathology progression.
studies.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) pathology is characterized by amyloid-β (Aβ) deposition and tau hyper-phosphorylation, accompanied by a progressive cognitive decline. Monocytes have been recently shown to play a major role in modulating Aβ pathology, and thereby have been pointed as potential therapeutic targets. However, the main challenge remains in identifying clinically relevant interventions that could modulate monocyte immune functions in absence of undesired off-target effects. Erythropoietin (EPO), a key regulator of erythrocyte production, has been shown to possess immunomodulatory potential and to provide beneficial effects in preclinical models of AD. However, the transition to use recombinant human EPO in clinical trials was hindered by unwanted erythropoietic effects that could lead to thrombosis. Here, we used a recently identified non-erythropoietic analogue of EPO, ARA 290, to evaluate its therapeutic potential in AD therapy. We first evaluated the effects of early systemic ARA 290 administration on AD-like pathology in an early-onset model, represented by young APP/PS1 mice. Our findings indicate that ARA 290 early treatment decelerated Aβ pathology progression in APP/PS1 mice while improving cognitive functions. ARA 290 potently increased the levels of total monocytes by specifically stimulating the generation of Ly6C<sup>Low</sup> patrolling subset, which are implicated in clearing Aβ from the cerebral vasculature, and subsequently reducing overall Aβ burden in the brain. Moreover, ARA 290 increased the levels of monocyte progenitors in the bone marrow. Using chimeric APP/PS1 mice in which Ly6C<sup>Low</sup> patrolling subset are selectively depleted, ARA 290 was inefficient in attenuating Aβ pathology and ameliorating cognitive functions in young animals. Interestingly, ARA 290 effects were compromised when delivered in a late-onset model, represented by aged APP1/PS1. In aged APP/PS1 mice in which AD-like pathology is at advanced stages, ARA 290 failed to reverse Aβ pathology and to increase the levels of circulating monocytes. Our study suggests that ARA 290 early systemic treatment could prevent AD-like progression via modulation of monocyte functions by specifically increasing the ratio of patrolling monocytes.

studies.title: A Nonhematopoietic Erythropoietin Analogue, ARA 290, Inhibits Macrophage Activation and Prevents Damage to Transplanted Islets.
studies.abstract: Erythropoietin exerts anti-inflammatory, antiapoptotic, and cytoprotective effects in addition to its hematopoietic action. A nonhematopoietic erythropoietin analogue, ARA 290, has similar properties. The efficacy of pancreatic islet transplantation (PITx) is reduced due to islet damage that occurs during isolation and from the severe inflammatory reactions caused by the transplantation procedure. We investigated whether ARA 290 protects islets and ameliorates inflammatory responses following PITx thus improving engraftment. The effects of ARA 290 on pancreatic islets of C57BL/6J (H-2) mice and on murine macrophages were investigated using an in vitro culture model. As a marginal PITx, 185 islets were transplanted into the liver of streptozotocin-induced diabetic mice (H-2) via the portal vein. Recipients were given ARA 290 (120 μg/kg) intraperitoneally just before and at 0, 6, and 24 hours after PITx. Liver samples were obtained at 12 hours after PITx, and expression levels of proinflammatory cytokines were assessed. ARA 290 protected islets from cytokine-induced damage and apoptosis. Secretion of pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-6, IL-12, and TNF-α) from macrophages was significantly inhibited by ARA 290. After the marginal PITx, ARA 290 treatment significantly improved the blood glucose levels when compared to those of control animals (P < 0.001). Upregulation of monocyte chemoattractant protein-1, macrophage inflammatory protein-1β, IL-1β, and IL-6 messenger RNA expression within the liver was suppressed by ARA 290 treatment. ARA 290 protected pancreatic islets from cytokine-induced damage and apoptosis and ameliorated the inflammatory response after PITx. ARA 290 appears to be a promising candidate for improvement of PITx.

studies.title: Erythropoietin-derived nonerythropoietic peptide ameliorates experimental autoimmune neuritis by inflammation suppression and tissue protection.
studies.abstract: Experimental autoimmune neuritis (EAN) is an autoantigen-specific T-cell-mediated disease model for human demyelinating inflammatory disease of the peripheral nervous system. Erythropoietin (EPO) has been known to promote EAN recovery but its haematopoiesis stimulating effects may limit its clinic application. Here we investigated the effects and potential mechanisms of an EPO-derived nonerythropoietic peptide, ARA 290, in EAN. Exogenous ARA 290 intervention greatly improved EAN recovery, improved nerve regeneration and remyelination, and suppressed nerve inflammation. Furthermore, haematopoiesis was not induced by ARA 290 during EAN treatment. ARA 290 intervention suppressed lymphocyte proliferation and altered helper T cell differentiation by inducing increase of Foxp3+/CD4+ regulatory T cells and IL-4+/CD4+ Th2 cells and decrease of IFN-γ+/CD4+ Th1 cells in EAN. In addition, ARA 290 inhibited inflammatory macrophage activation and promoted its phagocytic activity. In vitro, ARA 290 was shown to promote Schwann cell proliferation and inhibit its inflammatory activation. In summary, our data demonstrated that ARA 290 could effectively suppress EAN by attenuating inflammation and exerting direct cell protection, indicating that ARA 290 could be a potent candidate for treatment of autoimmune neuropathies.

This work highlights the value of touchscreen-based paradigms for resolving distinct cognitive domains in metabolic disease and highlights the need to target brain specific immunometabolic mechanisms to address diabetes-associated cognitive dysfunction.

studies.title: Early monocyte modulation by the non-erythropoietic peptide ARA 290 decelerates AD-like pathology progression.
studies.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) pathology is characterized by amyloid-β (Aβ) deposition and tau hyper-phosphorylation, accompanied by a progressive cognitive decline. Monocytes have been recently shown to play a major role in modulating Aβ pathology, and thereby have been pointed as potential therapeutic targets. However, the main challenge remains in identifying clinically relevant interventions that could modulate monocyte immune functions in absence of undesired off-target effects. Erythropoietin (EPO), a key regulator of erythrocyte production, has been shown to possess immunomodulatory potential and to provide beneficial effects in preclinical models of AD. However, the transition to use recombinant human EPO in clinical trials was hindered by unwanted erythropoietic effects that could lead to thrombosis. Here, we used a recently identified non-erythropoietic analogue of EPO, ARA 290, to evaluate its therapeutic potential in AD therapy. We first evaluated the effects of early systemic ARA 290 administration on AD-like pathology in an early-onset model, represented by young APP/PS1 mice. Our findings indicate that ARA 290 early treatment decelerated Aβ pathology progression in APP/PS1 mice while improving cognitive functions. ARA 290 potently increased the levels of total monocytes by specifically stimulating the generation of Ly6C

studies.title: A Nonhematopoietic Erythropoietin Analogue, ARA 290, Inhibits Macrophage Activation and Prevents Damage to Transplanted Islets.
studies.abstract:
Background

Erythropoietin exerts anti-inflammatory, antiapoptotic, and cytoprotective effects in addition to its hematopoietic action. A nonhematopoietic erythropoietin analogue, ARA 290, has similar properties. The efficacy of pancreatic islet transplantation (PITx) is reduced due to islet damage that occurs during isolation and from the severe inflammatory reactions caused by the transplantation procedure. We investigated whether ARA 290 protects islets and ameliorates inflammatory responses following PITx thus improving engraftment.

Methods

The effects of ARA 290 on pancreatic islets of C57BL/6J (H-2) mice and on murine macrophages were investigated using an in vitro culture model. As a marginal PITx, 185 islets were transplanted into the liver of streptozotocin-induced diabetic mice (H-2) via the portal vein. Recipients were given ARA 290 (120 μg/kg) intraperitoneally just before and at 0, 6, and 24 hours after PITx. Liver samples were obtained at 12 hours after PITx, and expression levels of proinflammatory cytokines were assessed.

Results

ARA 290 protected islets from cytokine-induced damage and apoptosis. Secretion of pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-6, IL-12, and TNF-α) from macrophages was significantly inhibited by ARA 290. After the marginal PITx, ARA 290 treatment significantly improved the blood glucose levels when compared to those of control animals (P < 0.001). Upregulation of monocyte chemoattractant protein-1, macrophage inflammatory protein-1β, IL-1β, and IL-6 messenger RNA expression within the liver was suppressed by ARA 290 treatment.

Conclusions

ARA 290 protected pancreatic islets from cytokine-induced damage and apoptosis and ameliorated the inflammatory response after PITx. ARA 290 appears to be a promising candidate for improvement of PITx.

studies.title: ARA 290 relieves pathophysiological pain by targeting TRPV1 channel: Integration between immune system and nociception.
studies.abstract: ARA 290 is an erythropoietin-derived polypeptide that possesses analgesic and tissue protective effect in many diseases such as diabetes and cancer. The analgesic effect of ARA 290 is mediated by its anti-inflammatory and immunomodulatory functions, or more specifically, by targeting the innate repair receptor (IRR) to down-regulate inflammation to alleviate neuropathic pain. However, whether other mechanisms or pathways are involved in ARA 290-mediated analgesic effect remains elusive. In this study, we are particularly interested in whether ARA 290 could directly target peripheral nociceptors by blocking or influencing receptors in pain sensation. Using calcium imaging, cell culture and behavioral tests, we demonstrated that ARA 290 was able to specifically inhibit TRPV1 channel activity, and relieve the mechanical hypersensitivity induced by capsaicin. Our study suggested that ARA 290 could potentially function as a novel antagonist for TRPV1 channel. This finding would not only contribute to the development of new pain treatment using ARA 290, but also help to improve our understanding of the integration between the immune system and the peripheral nervous system.

studies.title: Erythropoietin-derived nonerythropoietic peptide ameliorates experimental autoimmune neuritis by inflammation suppression and tissue protection.
studies.abstract: Experimental autoimmune neuritis (EAN) is an autoantigen-specific T-cell-mediated disease model for human demyelinating inflammatory disease of the peripheral nervous system. Erythropoietin (EPO) has been known to promote EAN recovery but its haematopoiesis stimulating effects may limit its clinic application. Here we investigated the effects and potential mechanisms of an EPO-derived nonerythropoietic peptide, ARA 290, in EAN. Exogenous ARA 290 intervention greatly improved EAN recovery, improved nerve regeneration and remyelination, and suppressed nerve inflammation. Furthermore, haematopoiesis was not induced by ARA 290 during EAN treatment. ARA 290 intervention suppressed lymphocyte proliferation and altered helper T cell differentiation by inducing increase of Foxp3+/CD4+ regulatory T cells and IL-4+/CD4+ Th2 cells and decrease of IFN-γ+/CD4+ Th1 cells in EAN. In addition, ARA 290 inhibited inflammatory macrophage activation and promoted its phagocytic activity. In vitro, ARA 290 was shown to promote Schwann cell proliferation and inhibit its inflammatory activation. In summary, our data demonstrated that ARA 290 could effectively suppress EAN by attenuating inflammation and exerting direct cell protection, indicating that ARA 290 could be a potent candidate for treatment of autoimmune neuropathies.

explanation.what_it_is_line: A short peptide derived from erythropoietin; targets immune and nerve signaling, not red blood cell production.
explanation.what_it_is: ARA-290 (also called Cibinetide) is a peptide — a short chain of amino acids — engineered from erythropoietin, a hormone your body naturally makes. Unlike the original hormone, which signals your bone marrow to produce red blood cells, ARA-290 has been redesigned to skip that effect and instead target immune cells and nerve endings. It is given by injection and is often used in research or clinical trials rather than as an approved medication.
explanation.how_it_works_line: Activates immune receptors on nerve cells and immune cells, reducing inflammation and pain signaling.
explanation.how_it_works: ARA-290 works by binding to specific receptors (docking points on cell surfaces) on immune cells and nerve endings — particularly a receptor called EPOR/CD131. When it binds, it dampens overactive immune responses and reduces the firing of pain-sensing neurons. In animal models, this has been shown to calm inflammation, ease pain signals in people with damaged small nerve fibers, and reduce immune-driven nerve damage. The peptide also appears to modulate how immune cells (especially macrophages — cells that patrol for infection and debris) behave, shifting them away from damage-promoting activity. The exact human mechanism is not yet fully mapped, but the principle is that it tells immune and nerve cells to 'turn down the alarm.'
explanation.safety_line: Mostly well-tolerated in short trials; long-term safety and interactions with other drugs remain untested.
explanation.safety_detail: The human trials that retrieved showed ARA-290 was generally tolerated without serious adverse events reported over the trial periods (typically weeks to a few months). However, these were small studies in specific patient populations (primarily people with sarcoidosis-related nerve damage). Because it is an injectable research peptide, potential for drug interactions, effects in pregnancy, kidney disease, and other unstudied populations is unknown.
safety_bullets: Long-term safety (beyond a few months) has not been established in retrieved human trials.
Not tested in pregnancy, kidney disease, liver disease, or adolescents — safety in these groups is unknown.
Potential drug interactions untested; use with other immune-modulating medications is uncharacterized.
explanation.chem_meaning: ARA-290 is a large, water-loving peptide (XLogP −7.7, very hydrophilic) made of 34 amino acids with a molecular weight of 1257 daltons. Its strong negative lipophilicity means it dissolves readily in water and does not cross cell membranes easily — it must bind to receptors on the cell surface, not enter the cell itself. This is why it must be injected rather than taken by mouth (stomach acid and the gut barrier would destroy it before it reached the bloodstream).

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Three human RCTs (2012–2015) in patients with sarcoidosis-related small nerve fiber neuropathy found that ARA-290 improved pain symptoms and increased corneal nerve fiber density (a marker of nerve repair). One animal study (2016) showed the peptide relieved pain in rodent models by targeting TRPV1 channels — receptors on pain-sensing neurons. The human trials involved roughly 22 verified participants across the measured studies and lasted weeks to months.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Human evidence exists but is small, limited to one disease (sarcoidosis), and rests on a narrow participant pool. This is promising, not yet conclusive.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Three human RCTs (2012–2015) in sarcoidosis patients reported improvements in metabolic control and blood sugar markers alongside neuropathy outcomes. Five animal studies (2014–2026) in models of diabetes and metabolic dysfunction showed ARA-290 reduced inflammation and altered immune cell behavior in ways that favor better glucose regulation. Human sample sizes were modest (~22 across verified trials), and the effect was reported alongside neuropathy outcomes rather than as a standalone glucose study.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Multiple human trials show a signal, supported by consistent animal findings. However, human evidence comes from small, single-disease trials not primarily designed to measure blood sugar; the effect estimate may be unstable and needs larger, dedicated studies.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: One human RCT (2013) in sarcoidosis patients reported reduced markers of inflammation alongside neuropathy improvement. Four animal studies (2014–2016) demonstrated that ARA-290 inhibits macrophage activation and reduces inflammatory cytokines (immune signaling molecules) in models of autoimmune nerve disease, metabolic dysfunction, and neurodegeneration.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Only one human study directly measures inflammation; no independent human replication exists. Animal data is consistent and mechanistically plausible, but human evidence is too thin to reach Moderate confidence.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Three human RCTs (2012–2015) in sarcoidosis patients reported cognitive or neurological outcomes as secondary endpoints. Five animal studies (2016–2026) in aging, Alzheimer's-like pathology, and autoimmune models showed that ARA-290 preserved cognitive function, modulated immune cells associated with neuroinflammation (especially monocytes), and reduced disease-like pathology progression. Human sample sizes remained modest (~22 across verified trials).
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Human trials are small and did not focus primarily on cognition; animal evidence is more extensive and mechanistically coherent. The human-animal signal aligns, but human evidence is limited in scope and sample size.

explanation.evidence_base: The evidence base consists of 3 human RCTs (conducted 2012–2015) primarily in patients with sarcoidosis-related small fiber neuropathy, plus 5 animal studies in diabetes, autoimmune, and neuroinflammatory models. All human trials were small (verified ~22 participants total in measured outcomes) and short-term (weeks to months). Animal studies are more recent (through 2026) and broader in scope. The confidence in human effects is limited by small sample size and narrow population (sarcoidosis); animal data is supportive but does not yet prove human benefit.
explanation.open_questions: The retrieved records show human trials only in sarcoidosis; whether ARA-290 helps people with other neuropathies, diabetes, or cognitive diseases is untested in humans. No long-term follow-up data (beyond a few months) was provided. No head-to-head comparisons with standard treatments appear in the records. Notably, three human trials (2012–2015) are relatively older; more recent human evidence may exist but was not in the sample retrieved. The small sample sizes mean a larger, dedicated trial in any single outcome would strengthen confidence.

appraisal.headline: All human evidence comes from a single trial (n=22, 2012) and its apparent follow-ups, so the entire clinical evidence base may represent one experimental population rather than independent replication—a critical transparency gap given the grey-market status and lack of regulatory approval.

concerns.issue: Single trial masquerading as multiple studies
concerns.detail: Across all four outcomes (neuropathic pain, blood sugar, inflammation, cognition), the human evidence is dominated by three RCTs with identical or near-identical titles and publication years (2012, 2013, 2015) describing the same sarcoidosis-related small fiber neuropathy population. The 2012 trial explicitly states n=22; the 2013 and 2015 papers appear to report the same cohort or overlapping subsets. No independent replication in a separate human population is visible in these records. This means every clinical grade rests on data from ~22 people studied once, not confirmation across separate trials.

concerns.issue: Heavy reliance on animal models with no human dose translation
concerns.detail: For blood sugar (5 of 8 studies animal), cognition (5 of 8 studies animal), and inflammation (4 of 5 studies animal), the evidence is predominantly preclinical. Animal models of db/db mice, experimental autoimmune neuritis, and AD-like pathology do not establish efficacy in human populations; they suggest a mechanism worthy of testing, not a clinically validated effect. The abstract records do not indicate whether animal doses were scaled to human-equivalent ranges, making mechanistic support for the clinical grades speculative.

concerns.issue: No sample sizes reported for majority of studies; imprecision unquantified
concerns.detail: Only 1 of 4 neuropathic pain studies, 1 of 8 blood sugar studies, and 0 of 5 inflammation studies report sample sizes in the abstracts provided. For cognition, only 1 of 8 studies is quantified. The engine correctly flags imprecision, but the true width of confidence intervals and risk of random error cannot be assessed from these records. A single human trial of n=22 has wide confidence intervals; without knowing if the supporting animal studies were adequately powered, the overall certainty is genuinely unknowable.

concerns.issue: Mechanism-to-outcome leap for blood sugar and cognition unvalidated
concerns.detail: The animal studies propose immune modulation (macrophage inhibition, monocyte modulation) and TRPV1 channel blockade as mechanisms. These plausibly link to neuropathic pain relief (a pain pathway target), but the jump from immune activation → improved glucose control or cognitive function in healthy humans is not demonstrated in the human trials. The 2015 RCT title mentions 'metabolic control' but the abstract does not clarify whether this refers to glycemic endpoints, insulin sensitivity, or surrogate measures in the sarcoidosis population. No mechanistic evidence in humans is provided for cognition.

concerns.issue: Grey-market status and approval gap unaddressed in evidence
concerns.detail: The compound is not approved for human use and is reportedly obtained grey-market. The clinical evidence is from 2012–2016, with no apparent regulatory pathway, follow-up safety studies, or recent confirmatory trials visible in the records. For a non-approved injectable peptide, the absence of modern pharmacovigilance data, long-term safety follow-up, or reproducibility attempts is a critical gap, especially given the small initial sample and sarcoidosis-specific population.

appraisal.mechanism_check: The immune modulation and TRPV1 inhibition mechanisms observed in animal models are plausible for neuropathic pain relief, since TRPV1 is a validated pain transduction target. However, the inference that immune modulation improves blood glucose control and cognition in humans relies entirely on the sarcoidosis trial outcomes, which are not detailed in these abstracts. No mechanistic bridge is provided between macrophage inhibition and the specific human endpoints claimed for blood sugar or cognition—the leap is inferential rather than experimentally supported in the human population.
appraisal.strongest_counterargument: A skeptic would note that all clinical evidence derives from a single n=22 trial in a disease-specific population (sarcoidosis with small fiber neuropathy), reported across three publications that appear to be the same or overlapping cohort. This is not independent replication; it is one study parsed into multiple papers. The supporting animal evidence, while suggestive of mechanism, does not validate efficacy in healthy humans or broader patient populations. Combined with the lack of regulatory approval, absence of recent confirmatory trials, and unpublished or grey-market status, the evidence base does not establish that ARA-290 produces the claimed benefits outside the narrow sarcoidosis population from which it was first studied.
appraisal.what_would_change_the_picture: An independent RCT in a different human population (e.g., diabetic neuropathy, or healthy volunteers for blood sugar/cognition) with n ≥ 100, published in a peer-reviewed venue post-2020, would provide genuine replication. Alternatively, a formal regulatory submission (IND, EMA) with transparent safety and efficacy data for a specified indication would establish whether the original trial findings are reproducible and whether the mechanism translates to humans outside the sarcoidosis context.

explanation_es.what_it_is_line: Un péptido corto derivado de la eritropoyetina; ataca la señalización inmunitaria y nerviosa, no la producción de glóbulos rojos.
explanation_es.what_it_is: ARA-290 (también llamado Cibinetide) es un péptido — una cadena corta de aminoácidos — diseñado a partir de la eritropoyetina, una hormona que su cuerpo produce naturalmente. A diferencia de la hormona original, que señala a la médula ósea para producir glóbulos rojos, ARA-290 ha sido rediseñado para omitir ese efecto y dirigirse en cambio a las células inmunitarias y terminaciones nerviosas. Se administra por inyección y se utiliza a menudo en investigación o ensayos clínicos en lugar de como medicamento aprobado.
explanation_es.how_it_works_line: Activa receptores inmunitarios en células nerviosas y células inmunitarias, reduciendo la inflamación y la señalización del dolor.
explanation_es.how_it_works: ARA-290 funciona uniéndose a receptores específicos (puntos de acoplamiento en las superficies celulares) en células inmunitarias y terminaciones nerviosas — particularmente un receptor llamado EPOR/CD131. Cuando se une, amortigua las respuestas inmunitarias excesivamente activas y reduce la activación de las neuronas sensoriales del dolor. En modelos animales, se ha demostrado que calma la inflamación, alivia las señales de dolor en personas con daño de fibras nerviosas pequeñas y reduce el daño nervioso causado por el sistema inmunitario. El péptido también parece modular cómo se comportan las células inmunitarias (especialmente los macrófagos — células que patrullan en busca de infección y desechos), desplazándolas lejos de la actividad promotora del daño. El mecanismo exacto en humanos aún no está completamente mapeado, pero el principio es que le dice a las células inmunitarias y nerviosas que 'bajen la alarma'.
explanation_es.safety_line: Generalmente bien tolerado en ensayos cortos; la seguridad a largo plazo y las interacciones con otros medicamentos permanecen sin evaluar.
explanation_es.safety_detail: Los ensayos en humanos recuperados mostraron que ARA-290 fue generalmente tolerado sin eventos adversos graves reportados durante los períodos de ensayo (típicamente semanas a algunos meses). Sin embargo, estos fueron estudios pequeños en poblaciones de pacientes específicos (principalmente personas con daño nervioso relacionado con sarcoidosis). Debido a que es un péptido de investigación inyectable, el potencial de interacciones farmacológicas, efectos en el embarazo, enfermedad renal y otras poblaciones no estudiadas es desconocido.
safety_bullets: La seguridad a largo plazo (más allá de algunos meses) no ha sido establecida en ensayos clínicos en humanos recuperados.
No probado en embarazo, enfermedad renal, enfermedad hepática o adolescentes — la seguridad en estos grupos es desconocida.
Posibles interacciones farmacológicas sin evaluar; el uso con otros medicamentos inmunorregu​ladores no está caracterizado.
explanation_es.chem_meaning: ARA-290 es un péptido grande y que ama el agua (XLogP −7,7, muy hidrofílico) compuesto por 34 aminoácidos con un peso molecular de 1257 daltons. Su fuerte lipofilicidad negativa significa que se disuelve fácilmente en agua y no cruza fácilmente las membranas celulares — debe unirse a receptores en la superficie celular, no penetrar la célula misma. Esta es la razón por la que debe ser inyectado en lugar de tomado por vía oral (el ácido del estómago y la barrera intestinal lo destruirían antes de que llegara al torrente sanguíneo).

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Tres ensayos clínicos aleatorizados en humanos (2012–2015) en pacientes con neuropatía de fibra nerviosa pequeña relacionada con sarcoidosis encontraron que ARA-290 mejoró los síntomas de dolor e aumentó la densidad de fibras nerviosas corneales (un marcador de reparación nerviosa). Un estudio animal (2016) mostró que el péptido alivió el dolor en modelos de roedores al dirigirse a los canales TRPV1 — receptores en neuronas sensoriales del dolor. Los ensayos en humanos involucraron aproximadamente 22 participantes verificados en los estudios medidos y duraron semanas a meses.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Existe evidencia en humanos pero es pequeña, limitada a una enfermedad (sarcoidosis) y descansa en un grupo de participantes estrecho. Esto es prometedor, pero aún no es concluyente.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Tres ensayos clínicos aleatorizados en humanos (2012–2015) en pacientes con sarcoidosis reportaron mejoras en el control metabólico y marcadores de azúcar en sangre junto con resultados de neuropatía. Cinco estudios animales (2014–2026) en modelos de diabetes y disfunción metabólica mostraron que ARA-290 redujo la inflamación y alteró el comportamiento de las células inmunitarias de maneras que favorecen una mejor regulación de la glucosa. Los tamaños de muestra en humanos fueron modestos (~22 en los ensayos verificados), y el efecto fue reportado junto con resultados de neuropatía en lugar de como un estudio de glucosa independiente.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Múltiples ensayos clínicos en humanos muestran una señal, apoyada por hallazgos animales consistentes. Sin embargo, la evidencia en humanos proviene de ensayos pequeños de una sola enfermedad no diseñados principalmente para medir azúcar en sangre; la estimación del efecto puede ser inestable y necesita ensayos más grandes y dedicados.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Un ensayo clínico aleatorizado en humanos (2013) en pacientes con sarcoidosis reportó marcadores reducidos de inflamación junto con mejora en la neuropatía. Cuatro estudios animales (2014–2016) demostraron que ARA-290 inhibe la activación de macrófagos y reduce las citocinas inflamatorias (moléculas de señalización inmunitaria) en modelos de enfermedad nerviosa autoinmune, disfunción metabólica y neurodegeneración.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Solo un estudio en humanos mide directamente la inflamación; no existe replicación humana independiente. Los datos animales son consistentes y mecánicamente plausibles, pero la evidencia en humanos es demasiado limitada para alcanzar confianza Moderada.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Tres ensayos clínicos aleatorizados en humanos (2012–2015) en pacientes con sarcoidosis reportaron resultados cognitivos o neurológicos como puntos finales secundarios. Cinco estudios animales (2016–2026) en envejecimiento, patología similar a Alzheimer y modelos autoinmunes mostraron que ARA-290 preservó la función cognitiva, moduló células inmunitarias asociadas con neuroinflammación (especialmente monocitos) y redujo la progresión de la patología similar a la enfermedad. Los tamaños de muestra en humanos permanecieron modestos (~22 en los ensayos verificados).
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Los ensayos en humanos son pequeños y no se enfocaron principalmente en cognición; la evidencia animal es más extensa y mecánicamente coherente. La señal humano-animal se alinea, pero la evidencia en humanos es limitada en alcance y tamaño de muestra.

explanation_es.evidence_base: La base de evidencia consiste en 3 ensayos clínicos aleatorizados en humanos (realizados 2012–2015) principalmente en pacientes con neuropatía de fibra pequeña relacionada con sarcoidosis, más 5 estudios animales en modelos de diabetes, autoinmune e inflamación neurológica. Todos los ensayos en humanos fueron pequeños (aproximadamente 22 participantes verificados en los resultados medidos) y a corto plazo (semanas a meses). Los estudios animales son más recientes (hasta 2026) y más amplios en alcance. La confianza en los efectos en humanos es limitada por el tamaño de muestra pequeño y la población estrecha (sarcoidosis); los datos animales son de apoyo pero aún no prueban el beneficio en humanos.
explanation_es.open_questions: Los registros recuperados muestran ensayos en humanos solo en sarcoidosis; si ARA-290 ayuda a personas con otras neuropatías, diabetes o enfermedades cognitivas no se ha probado en humanos. No se proporcionaron datos de seguimiento a largo plazo (más allá de algunos meses). No aparecen comparaciones cabeza a cabeza con tratamientos estándar en los registros. Notablemente, tres ensayos en humanos (2012–2015) son relativamente más antiguos; evidencia humana más reciente puede existir pero no estuvo en la muestra recuperada. Los tamaños de muestra pequeños significan que un ensayo más grande y dedicado en cualquier resultado único fortalecería la confianza.

appraisal_es.headline: Toda la evidencia en humanos proviene de un único ensayo (n=22, 2012) y sus aparentes seguimientos, por lo que toda la base de evidencia clínica podría representar una sola población experimental en lugar de replicación independiente—una brecha crítica de transparencia dado el estado de mercado gris y la falta de aprobación regulatoria.

concerns.issue: Un único ensayo haciéndose pasar por múltiples estudios
concerns.detail: En los cuatro resultados (dolor neuropático, glucosa en sangre, inflamación, cognición), la evidencia en humanos está dominada por tres ECA con títulos y años de publicación idénticos o casi idénticos (2012, 2013, 2015) que describen la misma población de neuropatía de fibra pequeña relacionada con sarcoidosis. El ensayo de 2012 explícitamente indica n=22; los artículos de 2013 y 2015 parecen informar la misma cohorte o subconjuntos superpuestos. No hay replicación independiente visible en una población humana separada en estos registros. Esto significa que cada calificación clínica se basa en datos de ~22 personas estudiadas una vez, no en confirmación en ensayos separados.

concerns.issue: Fuerte dependencia de modelos animales sin traducción de dosis humana
concerns.detail: Para glucosa en sangre (5 de 8 estudios en animales), cognición (5 de 8 estudios en animales) e inflamación (4 de 5 estudios en animales), la evidencia es predominantemente preclínica. Los modelos animales de ratones db/db, neuritis autoinmune experimental y patología similar a la enfermedad de Alzheimer no establecen eficacia en poblaciones humanas; sugieren un mecanismo digno de prueba, no un efecto clínicamente validado. Los registros de resúmenes no indican si las dosis en animales fueron escaladas a rangos equivalentes en humanos, lo que hace que el apoyo mecanístico para las calificaciones clínicas sea especulativo.

concerns.issue: Sin tamaños de muestra reportados para la mayoría de estudios; imprecisión no cuantificada
concerns.detail: Solo 1 de 4 estudios de dolor neuropático, 1 de 8 estudios de glucosa en sangre y 0 de 5 estudios de inflamación reportan tamaños de muestra en los resúmenes proporcionados. Para cognición, solo 1 de 8 estudios está cuantificado. El motor marca correctamente la imprecisión, pero el ancho verdadero de los intervalos de confianza y el riesgo de error aleatorio no pueden evaluarse desde estos registros. Un único ensayo humano de n=22 tiene intervalos de confianza amplios; sin saber si los estudios en animales de apoyo fueron adecuadamente potenciados, la certidumbre general es genuinamente desconocida.

concerns.issue: Salto mecanismo-a-resultado para glucosa en sangre y cognición no validado
concerns.detail: Los estudios en animales proponen modulación inmunológica (inhibición de macrófagos, modulación de monocitos) y bloqueo del canal TRPV1 como mecanismos. Estos se vinculan plausiblemente al alivio del dolor neuropático (un objetivo de la vía del dolor), pero el salto de activación inmunológica → control de glucosa mejorado o función cognitiva en humanos sanos no se demuestra en los ensayos humanos. El título del ECA de 2015 menciona 'control metabólico' pero el resumen no aclara si esto se refiere a objetivos glucémicos, sensibilidad a la insulina o medidas subrogadas en la población con sarcoidosis. No se proporciona evidencia mecanística en humanos para la cognición.

concerns.issue: Estado de mercado gris y brecha de aprobación no abordados en la evidencia
concerns.detail: El compuesto no está aprobado para uso en humanos y aparentemente se obtiene de mercado gris. La evidencia clínica es de 2012–2016, sin una vía regulatoria aparente, estudios de seguridad de seguimiento o ensayos confirmatorios recientes visibles en los registros. Para un péptido inyectable no aprobado, la ausencia de datos modernos de farmacovigilancia, seguimiento de seguridad a largo plazo o intentos de reproducibilidad es una brecha crítica, especialmente dada la muestra inicial pequeña y la población específica de sarcoidosis.

appraisal_es.mechanism_check: Los mecanismos de modulación inmunológica e inhibición de TRPV1 observados en modelos animales son plausibles para el alivio del dolor neuropático, ya que TRPV1 es un objetivo de transducción del dolor validado. Sin embargo, la inferencia de que la modulación inmunológica mejora el control de glucosa en sangre y la cognición en humanos se basa enteramente en los resultados del ensayo de sarcoidosis, que no se detallan en estos resúmenes. No se proporciona puente mecanístico entre la inhibición de macrófagos y los objetivos humanos específicos reclamados para glucosa en sangre o cognición—el salto es inferencial en lugar de estar experimentalmente apoyado en la población humana.
appraisal_es.strongest_counterargument: Un escéptico señalaría que toda la evidencia clínica proviene de un único ensayo n=22 en una población específica de enfermedad (sarcoidosis con neuropatía de fibra pequeña), reportado en tres publicaciones que parecen ser la misma cohorte u superpuesta. Esto no es replicación independiente; es un estudio dividido en múltiples artículos. La evidencia en animales de apoyo, aunque sugiere mecanismo, no valida la eficacia en humanos sanos o poblaciones de pacientes más amplias. Combinado con la falta de aprobación regulatoria, ausencia de ensayos confirmatorios recientes y estado no publicado o de mercado gris, la base de evidencia no establece que ARA-290 produce los beneficios reclamados fuera de la población estrecha de sarcoidosis de la que se estudió por primera vez.
appraisal_es.what_would_change_the_picture: Un ECA independiente en una población humana diferente (p. ej., neuropatía diabética, o voluntarios sanos para glucosa en sangre/cognición) con n ≥ 100, publicado en una revista revisada por pares posterior a 2020, proporcionaría replicación genuina. Alternativamente, una presentación regulatoria formal (IND, EMA) con datos de seguridad y eficacia transparentes para una indicación especificada establecería si los hallazgos del ensayo original son reproducibles y si el mecanismo se traduce a humanos fuera del contexto de sarcoidosis.
